title: Effects of doping on the enhanced electrocatalytic activity of Fe 2 O 3 -doped Bi 2 O 3  NPs for the degradation of organic dyes
content: This study focuses on fabricating Fe2O3-doped Bi2O3 NPs by the auto-combustion method as an effective electrocatalyst for degrading organic textile dyes, examining how different doping concentrations affect degradation efficiency for various dye types, e.g., cationic and anionic organic dyes. The study also examines the effect of multiple electrolytes (e.g., NaCl, Na2CO3, Na2SO4) on the overall degradation process and their influence on catalyst activity. Compared with pure Bi2O3 (74 nm), samples of 0.01Fe2O3-doped Bi2O3 (75 nm) and 1.0Fe2O3-doped Bi2O3 NPs (81 nm) NPs demonstrated superior electrocatalytic activity, with over 99% for EY and 92% for MB degradation within 18 and 30 min, with kinetic rate constants of 0.19297 min−1 and 0.09495 min−1, respectively. Reusability tests confirm structural stability after several cycles, as evidenced by X-ray diffraction (XRD) results after catalytic degradation. The cationic structure is more likely to be broken by high Fe2O3 doping concentrations, whereas the anionic structure is more likely to degrade at lower doping concentrations; therefore, it is crucial to consider how the concentration of Fe2O3 doping affects the degradation of dyes and other contaminants. Doping with Fe2O3 exhibited significant changes in the energy bandgap assessments, which enhanced performance in 0.01Fe2O3-doped Bi2O3 (3.86 eV) and 1.0Fe2O3-doped Bi2O3 NPs (3.84 eV), compared to pure Bi2O3 NPs (3.90 eV), and BET analysis revealed an average pore diameter of 4.09–10.31 nm.
